newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: GOVERNMENT AIMS TO RAISE NUMBER OF YEAR 12 STUDENTS
Federal Schools Minister, David Kemp, is aiming to raise the number of students finishing year 12 by increasing vocational education.
The Government has provided 187-million dollars in the budget for vocational education in secondary schools.
Dr Kemp's spokesman says the 65 percent of students don't go on to full-time tertiary education need a more relevant curriculum.
He says the aim is that it will motivate students to finish year 12 and also reduce the level of violence linked to students feeling bored and alienated.
FAMILY TAX PACKAGE LAUNCHED
The Federal Government has launched its billion dollar Family Tax Package in Sydney.
Under the initiative, which was one of the Coalition's key election commitments, families will receive an increase in their tax free threshold, or payments of up to 50 dollars a fortnight.
The benefits depend on the age and number of children in the family and the total household income.
During the unveiling, Prime Minister John Howard made an appeal for people to dig deep this Christmas and give to Charity.
$40,000 GOLD NUGGET FOUND
In the central Victorian gold fields, a prospector using a metal detector has found a 76 ounce gold nugget.
Valued at 40,000, the nugget was found about five centimetres beneath the ground near Ballarat.
The owner of the local Mining Exchange Gold Shop says the fossicker, who doesn't want to be identified, phoned him this morning to tell of another, smaller discovery.
He says he hasn't been told the exact location of the find because the prospector is still working the area.
PM CONDEMNED FOR IN-ACTION ON HANSON'S VIEWS
The Prime Minister has again been condemned for in-action on racial issues sparked by Independent MP Pauline Hanson.
New South Wales Magistrate, Pat O'Shane, says the John Howard's reluctance to repudiate the views of Ms Hanson is not good enough.
Magistrate O'Shane says Mr Howard's instead taking a populist view in order to cash in on the member for Oxley's support base.
She says the PM has ignored Aboriginal issues for years.
MARITIME UNION VOWS TO CONTINUE ACTION
The Maritime Union says it will continue its protest action against Indonesian ships and cargo in all Australian ports, which has already held up two ships in the Port of Newcastle.

Last week ships carrying wheat and steel products to Indonesia were delayed for 24 hours in Newcastle as part of action in support of two Indonesian trade union leaders, currently on trial in Jakarta.
Maritime union organiser, Jim Boyle says he can't predict when individual ships will be affected, but says the action is expected to continue for some time.
PORT LINCOLN WARNED ABOUT POSSIBLE RACIST TAG
The people of Port Lincoln in South Australia are being urged to rally against racism, or face the possibility of hurting the town's export tuna market.
South Australian Federal Liberal MP Chris Gallus says results of the weekend Council by-election could see the town labelled as racist.
Supporters of Mayor Peter Davis were elected in all five wards, with only four of the nine councillors who resigned over his controversial comments against multicuturalism, regaining their seats.
Ms Gallus says Port Lincoln residents should get together and issue a statement supporting multiculturalism and rejecting racism to avoid any adverse publicity or threats to the export market.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
